newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-LARA UNDER FIRE AS RELATIONS SOUR.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LARA UNDER FIRE AS RELATIONS SOUR.

text.p: Brian Lara came under fire from Australia captain Mark Taylor after West Indies won an ill-tempered fifth and final test by 10 wickets on Monday.
Taylor singled out Lara as the individual most responsible for whatever tension there might have been between the teams during the series, which Australia had already clinched before the final test.
Relations deteriorated to such an extent on Monday that umpires Darrell Hair and Peter Willey took the unusual step of warning both sides about their behaviour at the WACA Ground.
West Indies won inside three days on their favourite ground in Australia, although it was not enough to prevent Taylor's side winning the series 3-2 and retaining the Frank Worrell trophy.
The umpires delivered their message to both Taylor and West Indies captain Courtney Walsh during play after a number of verbal exchanges between rival players in the middle.
Taylor said relations between the two teams were generally good, with one notable exception.
"I think he (Lara) is an antagonist. He looks for things to happen. It gets him going and it gets other people away from their game. He does it very well," Taylor told reporters.
Lara accused the Australians of persistent sledging on Sunday after he scored his only century of an otherwise deeply disappointing test series.

In his comments, Taylor referred specifically to Lara's behaviour during the second test in Sydney in December when Lara stormed into the Australian dressing-room to protest about the circumstances surrounding his dismissal.

"(During the series) there has only been one incident that has been damaging in any way to the game and that happened in Sydney and involved the man who was making the allegations (of sledging)," said Taylor, who has endured a miserable series as an opener, averaging just 17.
"I think the sides get on well, you see we are only talking about one individual."
West Indies began the third day on 353 for seven and moved to 384 all out in reply to Australia's 243 before dismissing the home side for 194 in their second innings.
That left the tourists with a target of 54 runs for victory, a task which openers Sherwin Campbell and Robert Samuels achieved with ease in 44 minutes and 10.2 overs.

Veteran fast bowler Walsh, who was making his final appearance in Australia, said: "I think the series result is a true reflection of how the teams played but I am delighted that we came back the way we did today."
Walsh bowled throughout the afternoon session to claim five wickets despite a painful hamstring injury in his right leg.
"The team required for someone to stay there and fight a bit," said Walsh, who exploited the extreme and variable bounce in the WACA wicket to rout Australia's middle order.
"It did hurt and I was getting a bit worried about it but five or six of the guys asked me to keep going bowling and it was hard to tell them no'," Walsh said.
Walsh was batting, with Lara as a runner, when he was summoned with Taylor to speak to the umpires.

International Cricket Council match referee Raman Subba Row said in a statement: "The umpires said there was a fair bit of niggle from both sides and they told the captains, enough was enough'," Subba Row said in a statement.
